title: FP8 stability scoreboard and cross-batch calibration orchestration for Hopper (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Safely enable FP8 (E4M3 / E5M2) quantization profiles for Hopper-based fleets with an automated, observable activation path that minimizes accuracy regressions across customers and workloads. This ticket builds an FP8 Stability Scoreboard, a cross-batch calibration orchestration layer, and an activation policy (hysteresis + model classifier) that picks E4M3 vs E5M2 per-model and per-workload bucket. Deliverables: 1) Stability Scoreboard service that aggregates per-model per-shard metrics (delta-EMB, LM perplexity delta, token-level hallucination heuristics) and computes a multi-dimensional stability score; 2) Cross-batch calibration orchestrator that (a) runs synthetic stress suites across representative batches, (b) computes per-layer scale factors with weighted smoothing across time windows, and (c) emits golden calibration manifests; 3) Activation policy implementing rolling-hysteresis, dynamic fallback to INT8, and shadow-canary traffic routing; 4) Observability and alerting: dashboards, regression gates, and automated rollback playbook for detected drifts. Rationale: Prior attempts toggled FP8 at coarse granularity and relied on single-shot calibration that drifted under cross-batch distribution changes. This design emphasizes continuously validated calibration with conservative activation heuristics and explicit per-model profiles to reduce customer-facing regressions.
comments: 2025-02-13 — Kickoff: Defined scope with RD and MLEs. Agreed on stability score dimensions: accuracy delta (eval seed set), distribution drift index, failed-token-rate, and latency delta under FP8 paths.

2025-02-15 — Prototype: Data team produced synthetic stress suite (token-length skew, prefix-heavy, rare-token injection). Initial runs show E4M3 has lower bias on long-prefix regimes; E5M2 is slightly better on short-seq throughput cases.

2025-02-18 — Design decision: Use classifier-based profile selector (lightweight decision tree) that favors E4M3 for long-context/chatty workloads and E5M2 for short-batch high-throughput workloads. Classifier trained on microbenchmarks and production sample traces.
2025-02-20 — Telemetry: Added additional histogram buckets for cross-batch scale variance and per-op quantization saturation counts. These metrics are required gating signals for canary promotion.

2025-02-22 — Implementation: Stability Scoreboard service scaffolded (metrics ingestion, per-model aggregation, score calc). First public API: /scoreboard/v1/models/{model}/scores returning JSON (internal contract agreed).

2025-02-24 — Testing: Ran shadow canary on 5 models (gpt-medium-*-open, rtx-native-37). Observed one regression on summarization dataset — root cause traced to per-layer outlier in attention projection; fallback rule triggered and traffic routed back to INT8 for that model.

2025-02-25 — Review feedback from ML reliability: Add feature to compute rolling stability delta over windows [T-1h, T-24h, T-7d] and require monotonic improvement before activation. Also require end-to-end evals on customer-supplied prompt-sets if available.
2025-02-27 — Ops checklist added: pre-activation snapshot of model weights, golden calibration manifest, and synthetic stress artifacts archived for later forensic debugging.
2025-02-28 — Next: Complete PR for orchestrator (runtime PR referenced), implement automated rollback runbook steps in Console, and schedule a 1% global canary for 03/03 pending final QA sign-off.
runbook: Canary plan: 0.5% shadow -> 0.5% live -> 1% live -> 5% live with 2-hour observation windows and automated metric gates.
Gating thresholds: stability_score >= 0.92 for promotion; EM delta <= 0.6% absolute; failed-token-rate increase <= 0.1ppt; latency p95 <= baseline + 10ms.
Fallback: Immediate route to INT8 or previous trusted quant profile. If score drops by > 0.06 in any window, trigger auto-rollback and page on-call.
Incident steps: collect golden-manifest, latest calibration parameters, run synthetic stress suite locally, capture per-op saturation histograms and KV cache hit-rates.
Communication: update status channel #runtime-fp8 with brief incident notes and link to scoreboard dashboard and PRs.
Postmortem requirements: classify regression type (calibration noise vs model sensitivity vs kernel numerical instability) and attach corrective action to the ticket.
Manual abort: engineers can abort rollout via admin console toggle; must include short justification note for audit logs.
Safety windows: no promotions within 48h of a patch-level runtime upgrade unless explicitly approved by release lead.
qa_plan: Regression harness: run the golden-suite (1000 seeded prompts) across E4M3, E5M2, and INT8 and compare token-level diffs and a downstream QA checkpoint suite (summarization, codegen, Q&A).
A/B quality evals: use human eval panel for 3 highest-risk models (5 prompts each) with blind comparisons between baseline and FP8-enabled outputs.
Stress tests: run extreme batch-size and prefix-length permutations to surface saturation and pooling issues.
CI gating: add end-to-end calibration validation job to CI with synthetic seed to ensure deterministic calibration artifacts are reproducible.
Acceptance criteria: no statistically significant degradation on seeded evals and stability_score >= threshold for 72h under shadow traffic.
